Definition: from G3080 and ἀνία (trouble); grief-dispelling; Lysanias, a governor of Abilene:--Lysanias.
BiblicalUsage: Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene, and Luke names him among the rulers of the day when John the Baptist began his ministry, in the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar. His name fixes the gospel in real history, under real governors.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Lysanias matters because Luke dated the gospel by rulers like him, and the good news entered history, not a fairy tale.
